latest_release.name: rig-v0.47.0
latest_release.body:
### Added

- *(rig-basics, rig-memory, rig-ecs, rig-core)* [**breaking**] compaction has no undo: the `Uncompact` event, `undo_summary`, `Uncompacted` and `UndoError` are removed, and with them the `/uncompact` command built on them; the replaced messages stay visible in the transcript. `Recovering` is removed, and `Summarizing::keep_from` is replaced by `replaces`. `apply_summary` takes the messages the compaction read and replaces exactly those, only while unchanged. Summary calls are retried by the kernel as `[retry]` says and after the wait the provider asks for; a blank summary fails (`SummaryFailure::Empty`). `StopTurn::plugin_done` ends a plugin's own turn and lets queued messages carry it on. A provider error code listed as final (`insufficient_quota` and the like) is not retried, whatever the HTTP status ([#3436](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/3436)) (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper))
- *(rig-memory, rig-basics, rig-ecs)* [**breaking**] compaction works as in the pi coding agent: it keeps about 20k tokens of the newest messages, never splitting a tool exchange, and updates the previous summary with pi's prompts (in rig-memory) in a separate call. It compacts and resends once after a context-overflow refusal or a reply the window cut short, and refuses an errored or cut-off summary with the reason. `[compaction]` takes `enabled`, `reserve_tokens` and `keep_recent_tokens`; `keep_recent`, `keep_asked`, `clearing`, `near_window`, `prompts`, `limits` and `tracked` are gone and refused as unknown. Old tool outputs are no longer cleared. rig-memory's compaction policy, summarizer and output-clearing API (`CompactionPolicy`, `Summarizer`, `SummaryPrompts`, `SummaryLimits`, `ClearToolOutputs`, `TrackArgument`, …) is replaced by pure functions (`prepare_compaction`, `find_cut_point`, `summary_request`, `summarization_request`, `summary_text`, …), and `ErrorReport::context_overflow` is removed ([#3434](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/3434)) (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper))
- *(rig-basics, rig-tui, rig-harness, rig-harness-protocol, rig-cli, rig-steel, rig-ecs)* [**breaking**] forks and rewind (`/fork`, Alt+Up then Enter) are `sessions::forks::ForksPlugin`, renamed from `sessions::agents::AgentsPlugin`, and off by default; `rig plugin enable rig_basics::sessions::forks::ForksPlugin` turns them on. `/agents` is its own plugin, `agent_picker::AgentPickerPlugin`, off by default and added by forks and subagents; `AgentColumn`, `ColumnOf` and `AgentColumns` moved to `rig_basics::agent_picker`. The status line, the key hints, the terminal title with its OSC 133 marks, and the working animation are default plugins that can be turned off (`rig_tui::status::StatusLinePlugin`, `rig_tui::hints::KeyHintsPlugin`, `rig_tui::title::TerminalTitlePlugin`, `rig_basics::activity::animation::WorkingAnimationPlugin`); `rig_tui::TuiPlugin` is the bare view and the new `rig_tui::TuiPlugins` group adds the three parts to it, so an app that added `TuiPlugin` itself adds `TuiPlugins` to keep them; `[tui] mark_nonce_env` is now `[title] mark_nonce_env`, and `[status] hide = [..]` leaves status-line parts out by name. `/plugins` is a tree of crates, areas and plugins, with the status line's parts under it. Steel is a pure code mode: `spawn-agent`, `send` and `reply` work only with Subagents on. With nothing saved or named, the terminal view starts on the same automatic model pick as print mode and ACP, which takes the ChatGPT plan's default model first when you are signed in. `PickItem` gains `parent`. A command refused because a turn is running comes back in the input with the reason, and a plugin that panics while the agent starts shows its panic message in the rebuild error ([#3425](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/3425)) (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper))
- *(rig-harness-protocol, rig-cli, rig-basics)* `[plugins] off` turns off branc

detail.readme: [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rig.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rig) [![docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/rig)](https://docs.rs/rig) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/511303648119226382?label=Discord)](https://discord.gg/playgrounds) Rig is a Rust library for building applications on large language models. It also ships `rig`, a terminal coding agent built on the library that you extend with Bevy plugins. ## The coding agent ```bash cargo install rig rig ``` This installs the launcher of the latest release. Each release's guide is on its tag, such as [0.47.0's guide](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/blob/v0.47.0/docs/agent.md). The [agent guide](docs/agent.md#install-and-run) on `main` can be ahead of the release, and shows how to install `main` from a checkout. The agent needs Rust 1.97.1 or newer and runs on Linux and macOS. The first `rig` builds the agent, which takes several minutes, and opens it. Run `/login` to sign in or save an API key, or export one such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` before starting. `/model` picks a model and `/help` lists the commands. `rig -p "fix the failing test"` answers one prompt and exits. Its tools, commands, sessions, sign-in and terminal view are each a plugin, so any of them can be turned off, replaced or added to. `/reload` rebuilds the agent with your changes and keeps the session. - The [agent guide](docs/agent.md) covers updating, models, sessions, tools, settings and scripting. - The [plugin guide](crates/rig-harness/PLUGINS.md) explains the basics of a plugin and points at working examples of each kind. ## The library ```bash cargo add rig anyhow cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread ``` ```rust use rig::prelude::*; use rig::providers::openai::{self, OpenAI}; #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> { // Reads OPENAI_API_KEY. let model = OpenAI::from_env()?.completion(openai::GPT_6_2_SOL); let agent = AgentBuilder::new(model) .preamble("You are a comedian.") .build(); let response = agent.prompt("Entertain me!").await?; println!("{}", response.output()); Ok(()) } ``` Rig puts over 20 model providers and a dozen vector stores behind one interface. It has agents with tools, streaming and typed hooks. It covers completion, embedding, transcription, audio and image models and follows the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions. `rig-core` and `rig-agent` build for browser WASM. See [`examples/`](examples), the [guides](https://rig.rs/docs) and the [API reference](https://docs.rs/rig). ## Crates The `rig` crate re-exports `rig-core`. Its default features add `rig-agent`, the derive macros, the reqwest HTTP client with rustls and, on native targets, the `rig` launcher (feature `cli`, from `rig-cli`); `default-features = false` leaves them out. Each crate in the list below is a feature named after it without `rig-`: ```bash cargo add rig --features memory,fastembed ``` - Agents and state: [`rig-agent`](crates/rig-agent), [`rig-memory`](crates/rig-memory) (saved conversations), [`rig-cassette`](crates/rig-cassette) (record and replay), [`rig-rmcp`](crates/rig-rmcp) (MCP tools). - Models: [`rig-bedrock`](crates/rig-bedrock), [`rig-vertexai`](crates/rig-vertexai), [`rig-gemini-grpc`](crates/rig-gemini-grpc), [`rig-candle`](crates/rig-candle) (local models), [`rig-fastembed`](crates/rig-fastembed) (local embeddings), [`rig-typesafeai`](crates/rig-typesafeai) (TypeSafe Jev judgments). The vector stores, such as LanceDB, Qdrant and PostgreSQL, are companion crates behind features too; [docs.rs lists every feature](https://docs.rs/crate/rig/latest/features). Internals: [`rig-core`](crates/rig-core) (messages, models, tools, providers), [`rig-derive`](crates/rig-derive) (feature `derive`), [`rig-http`](crates/rig-http) (transport traits), [`rig-reqwest`](crates/rig-reqwest) (feature `reqwest`) and [`rig-tungstenite`](crates/rig-tungstenite) (feature `websocket`). Coding agent: [`rig-cli`](crates/rig-cli) (feature `cli`, the library of the `rig` binary) and, not facade features, [`rig-harness`](crates/rig-harness), [`rig-harness-protocol`](crates/rig-harness-protocol), [`rig-ecs`](crates/rig-ecs), [`rig-tools`](crates/rig-tools), [`rig-markdown`](crates/rig-markdown), and the plugins [`rig-basics`](plugins/rig-basics), [`rig-tui`](plugins/rig-tui), [`rig-fold`](plugins/rig-fold), [`rig-steel`](plugins/rig-steel), [`rig-mcp-client`](plugins/rig-mcp-client), [`rig-acp`](plugins/rig-acp), [`rig-inspect`](plugins/rig-inspect), [`rig-traffic`](plugins/rig-traffic) and [`rig-bridge`](plugins/rig-bridge). ## Community Ask questions on [Discord](https://discord.gg/playgrounds). [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) says how to contribute, and [awesome-rig](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/awesome-rig) lists projects built on Rig. Rig is pre-1.0, so releases break APIs. The [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [migration notes](MIGRATING.md) say what changed. Rig is MIT licensed.
